main_text.p: forti & duro, fortius aut durius excogi-tari possit, dignum illud omne, quod in tale humani generis monstrum effun-datur: imò, ipse dignus qui secum in morte socios habeat, quorum in vita sese imitatorem oftendit. quod olim etiam in parricidæ supplicio factitatum perhibetur, *Cuius supplicio non debuit unà parari. Simia nec ser-pens unus nec culeus unus, luve. Sat.8,gallum scilicet, viperam, simiam, & canem; gallum, quia ut ifte parentem suum aggredi non veretur, ita nec Regicida tàm suum quàm patriæ communem parentem; viperam, quia ipsius viscera corrodit, cujus beneficio luce fruitur; simiam, quia cùm externam hominis figuram gestet, vilis-sima bestia deteriorem animum induit; canem denique, ut hujus animalis in suum dominum fidelitas hujusmodi portenti condemnat perfidiam. Caii Cæsaris exemplum nobis erit instar omnium, quod eo libentiùs è propha-[?] na Historia profero, quia in sequenti- bus me paulò strictiùs intra ecclesiasti- cæ limites statui compingere. Hic itaque licet vi & armis statum illius Reip. ad unius principatum evexerit, ejus tamen percussores omnes, qui nihilominùs

page.notes: The marginal note carries the mark "*", which stands in the text before "gallum". Its text is partly italic. The last line of this part is cut off at the bottom of the scan, so the transcription ends there. The word "propha-" at the line end is uncertain; the scan is faint there. The first line is a fragment of a sentence continued from the previous part of the page.
